criterion: Generalization ratio G = F1_APTOS / F1_EyePACS >= 0.85, and pipeline > baseline
evaluation_dataset: APTOS 2019 (3,662 images, mixed cameras, Indian population)
protocol: Zero-shot transfer — no retraining on APTOS 2019
checkpoints: EfficientNet-B3, fold-0 only (Configs A/B were not evaluated on APTOS)
caveats: The baseline also clears the G >= 0.85 threshold (0.8577), so that criterion on its own does not separate the arms — the discriminating part of H-4 is 'better than baseline'. The honest phrasing is that the pipeline does not rescue transfer, it improves transfer that was already acceptable.
G is normalized by each arm's own in-domain F1, so the stronger arm carries a larger denominator: delta-G (+0.040) is a deliberately conservative view of an absolute APTOS gain of +0.089.
Evaluated from fold-0 checkpoints; there is no between-fold variance for this experiment, and the 95% CIs are per-instance bootstrap intervals.
The gain is present on all five DR grades; macro-F1 rises more than weighted F1 (+0.102 vs +0.089), so it is concentrated on the minority grades.
